title: AvalonBridge Channel - GPU SaaS Partner Intro
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Avalon Bridge to explore a channel/reseller integration for Avalon Bridge's GPU-backed SaaS offering. Discussed integration surfaces (API keys, marketplace, reseller pricing), deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance requirements (SOC 2, SSO, KMS), and next steps around pilot scope and benchmarking. Action items include sharing security docs, proposal for pilot pricing, and scheduling a follow-up technical deep dive and bench run.
topics: deployment modes and constraints (VPC, dedicated GPU, on-prem)
security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Avalon Bridge Head Partnerships), Liam O'Shea (Avalon CTO), Devon Keller (Avalon Solutions Architect)

00:00 Sophie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie with Redwood Inference, AE on the partner org. Marcus my SE is here too.
00:08 Rina Patel: Hi Sophie, thanks—excited to learn more. Quick note, we're on a tight timeline for a marketplace launch in Q2.
00:15 Marcus Ortiz: Awesome, we'll keep it practical. Real quick can you outline what Avalon Bridge is shipping today?
00:21 Liam O'Shea: Sure, so Avalon Bridge runs a managed GPU SaaS that hosts inference endpoints for our vertical apps—image, vector search, and some custom large model ops. We do multi-tenant with per-customer networking isolation; customers buy through our marketplace or direct. We're looking for a partner to provide a low-friction model serving layer and routing options, plus co-sell motions.
00:41 Devon Keller: And technically we're using a mix of on-prem racks and cloud GPUs right now, NVIDA A100 and some H100 tests. We also do a lot of KV cache / prefix caching in our service, so inference latency and memory mgmt matter.
01:01 Sophie Chen: Great, that's helpful. Two buckets today—go-to-market/channel mechanics and technical integration. On GTM, are you planning to resell Redwood-hosted endpoints or do you want Redwood tech embedded in your stack?
01:12 Rina Patel: Prefer reseller model initially—Avalon lists the offering in our marketplace and we handle billing. But long term we'd like an OEM or white-label private deployment too.
01:24 Marcus Ortiz: That maps to our Dedicated and Private offerings—dedicated pools for predictable throughput or a private instance if you need VPC/on-prem control. Question on compliance: do you need SOC 2 or more?
01:36 Liam O'Shea: SOC 2 is baseline, and several customers demand KMS-backed key management and region-locking for data residency. Also SAML SSO for admin console.
01:48 Sophie Chen: Yep, we have SOC 2 Type II and KMS integrations; for private deployments we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM. I'll share security pack after the call.
01:56 Devon Keller: Great. On networking—how would routing work? We want requests from our marketplace to go to Redwood but keep audit logs and traces correlated with our tenant IDs.
02:08 Marcus Ortiz: We can surface request metadata and token-level tracing; we support custom headers for tenant mapping and can instrument trace IDs back to your systems. There may be small additional metadata payloads for routing or cost attribution.
02:28 Rina Patel: Pricing model question—do you do reseller discounts or revenue share?
02:33 Sophie Chen: We typically do committed reserved capacity for partners with channel pricing—either a percentage share or wholesale per-token rates depending on commit level. We can draft a channel pricing proposal for your expected volume.
02:46 Liam O'Shea: We're expecting initial pilots ~50–100 qps sustained with spikes to 300 for launches. Latency SLO target is P95 < 250 ms for embedding-style requests, but for some generations we can accept higher latency if cost savings are significant.
03:08 Marcus Ortiz: Good to know. For embeddings that's easy to keep low; for larger gen workloads we can recommend quantized variants and batching policies to balance cost/latency.
03:22 Devon Keller: You mentioned quantization—do you have recommended profiles for H100 vs A100 vs Ampere? We care about model parity after quantizing.
03:33 Marcus Ortiz: We publish quantization profiles per architecture. For H100 you'll see different kernel paths; we can share benchmark outputs. There is sometimes minor quality delta at aggressive quantization, so we recommend A/B tests on your datasets.
03:50 Rina Patel: On the marketplace integration, can Redwood appear as a labeled provider in our UI and support click-to-provision? Or do we need to manage provisioning on our side?
03:58 Sophie Chen: Both—our API supports programmatic provisioning plus marketplace connectors. For reseller, we can do provisioning through a marketplace webhook flow so customers can spin up endpoints and you still own billing.
04:12 Liam O'Shea: Any constraints on tenant isolation? We need cryptographic isolation between tenants for certain customers.
04:20 Marcus Ortiz: For Dedicated we provision GPU pools per partner/customer and we have node-level isolation; for Private we can go full VPC with customer-managed networking and K8s namespaces or even air-gapped on-prem if required.
04:40 Devon Keller: Important: audit log retention must be 1 year for a couple of healthcare customers. Is that configurable?
04:46 Sophie Chen: Yes, audit retention is configurable; longer retention is an add-on. We also deliver per-request logs and traces.
04:53 Rina Patel: Cool. Switching to technical: could we run a short benchmark—say embedding throughput and latency—before committing? We'd like to compare Redwood-hosted against our current pipeline.
05:05 Marcus Ortiz: Absolutely. Typical partner bench flow: we run a 48–72 hour bench with representative workloads, include KV/prefix caching scenarios, and deliver a token-level cost/latency report plus suggested batching configs. You'll need to provide sample prompts/datasets and target QPS.
05:25 Liam O'Shea: We can provide a dataset and representative request patterns. Can you run the bench against both hosted and a dedicated pool?
05:33 Marcus Ortiz: Yes, we can. Hosted bench will be quickest; dedicated bench requires reserving capacity but we can spin a small dedicated pool for the test window.
05:44 Devon Keller: Anything we should be aware of re: rate limits or request shaping for the bench?
05:48 Marcus Ortiz: We'll mirror your target QPS; only caveat is we ask you not to start other heavy workloads in the same tenant during bench. We'll provide a small runbook.
06:00 Rina Patel: From partnership side, what enablement materials do you provide? We need onboarding docs, SDK snippets, and co-marketing assets.
06:07 Sophie Chen: We'll provide an integration kit—API docs, sample SDKs for node/python, a checklist for marketplace integration, and a partner marketing one-pager. Also we can do a joint webinar once we have customer stories.
06:21 Liam O'Shea: A few concerns from procurement—data residency clauses in our contract, indemnity, and audit rights. Do you support contract redlines?
06:30 Sophie Chen: Yes, our legal team does partner redlines for channel agreements; we can share a standard partner agreement. For residency we have region-specific hosting and private options.
06:42 Devon Keller: Security deep-dive later will need architecture diagrams. Can your SE produce a draft network diagram showing VPC peering and flow?
06:50 Marcus Ortiz: I can produce that. For private deployments we'll show a diagram with customer VPC, NATs, egress controls, and KMS integration points.
06:59 Sophie Chen: Let's table next a quick run through technical constraints: model onboarding—how do you expect model versions to be surfaced in marketplace?
07:08 Rina Patel: We want clear version labels, compatibility notes, and an easy way to pin versions per-customer. Also a rollback mechanism if a model causes regressions.
07:19 Marcus Ortiz: We support model version pinning and can do canary rollouts per tenant; rollbacks are supported and we can tie rollouts to evals to catch quality regressions.
07:31 Liam O'Shea: On cost—how granular is billing, per token or per request? We may want to show cost to our customers in our billing UI.
07:40 Sophie Chen: Token-level billing is standard; we can provide per-request breakdowns and cost attribution metadata so you can surface it in your UI.
07:51 Rina Patel: Do you have marketplace listing examples from other partners?
07:54 Sophie Chen: Yes—I'll share examples from a couple of existing channel partners (anonymized).
08:00 Devon Keller: Technical nit: do you expose KV cache control to the caller or is that internal? For interactive sessions we need to control prefixes.
08:10 Marcus Ortiz: You can manage cache control via request headers and we have APIs to pre-warm KV caches for predictable patterns.
08:19 Liam O'Shea: About latency: you mentioned smart routing earlier—can we route requests to cheaper regions during low-load and fall back to dedicated in high-load?
08:28 Marcus Ortiz: Yes, routing policies configurable by latency/cost/region/customer tier. Automatic fallback to compatible model variants is built-in.
08:38 Rina Patel: Are there any gotchas for multi-tenant licensing—if we resell, does Redwood require naming customers?
08:45 Sophie Chen: We typically need customer IDs for billing reconciliation; we can accept hashed IDs if you need privacy but we'll need enough metadata for audits.
08:55 Liam O'Shea: Any restrictions on model licensing? We have a few proprietary models—can they be hosted on Redwood Dedicated or Private?
09:03 Marcus Ortiz: Proprietary models can live on Dedicated or Private; for hosted public catalog we curate open models. For private/OEM we support private model deployment with contract controls.
09:16 Devon Keller: Ok, that's helpful. Can we also get an estimate for latency under a 300 qps spike scenario for a 2k-token generation? Even a ballpark will help sizing.
09:27 Marcus Ortiz: Ballpark: on A100 with proper batching you'd probably see P95 in 600–900 ms for 2k tokens under spike, H100 might be 30–40% faster depending on kernels; we'll bench this for you to get accurate numbers.
09:44 Rina Patel: Competitive question—are you seeing partners use third-party runtime lairs or is Redwood positioned as the runtime?
09:50 Sophie Chen: We see both—some partners embed our runtime for deep OEMs; others prefer to resell hosted endpoints. Competitors mentioned in our space: PineCloud, NimbusAI, and BlackPeak—each has different tradeoffs.
10:04 Liam O'Shea: Procurement will want to see SLAs—uptime and latency SLOs for dedicated customers?
10:10 Sophie Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include draft SLA terms in the partner packet.
10:18 Devon Keller: Are there any preliminary integration blockers you foresee from the Redwood side?
10:22 Marcus Ortiz: Nothing obvious; we may need to scope the marketplace webhook contract and billing reconciliation if you have custom flows.
10:30 Rina Patel: Next steps idea: 1) Security docs and partner agreement; 2) Pilot scope and benchmark plan; 3) Tech deep dive with detailed diagram and bench kickoff.
10:40 Sophie Chen: That works—I'll capture those as action items.
10:45 Liam O'Shea: Timeline: can we aim to start bench in three weeks? We need time to prep datasets.
10:50 Sophie Chen: Three weeks is doable. We'll propose dates after we share the bench runbook.
10:55 Devon Keller: One last question: you'd support SAML for SSO to our admin console for partner-level controls, right?
10:59 Sophie Chen: Yes SAML SSO supported; we'll include SSO config docs.
11:05 Rina Patel: Ok thanks—this was productive.
11:08 Sophie Chen: Thank you all. We'll follow up with security pack, partner pricing proposal, and avail for a technical deep dive.
11:14 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional speaker overlaps and minor transcription errors (e.g., "NVIDA" for "NVIDIA" or "lairs" for "layers").
